title: Power Platform governance: multi-grader comparison for agent evaluations
summary: The briefing passes: its roadmap facts, comparison path and evaluation API match the sources checked. The statement that the new comparison shows agent responses is not established by those sources; the signed-in-profile statement should also be scoped to the preview experience it documents.

claims.claim: For existing evaluations, only the maker who initiated the test run can view agent responses and result explanations.
claims.quote: Makers can see the run status and result metrics of any test run, but only the maker who initiated the test run can view the agent responses and result explanations.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: The preview Evaluate experience shows estimated Copilot Credit usage, including at the individual test-case level.
claims.quote: You can see which experiences use credits, an estimated total for each evaluation run, a breakdown between generating and scoring responses, and credit usage at the individual test-case level.

claims.claim: For the Microsoft Copilot harness, generating and creating agent evaluations consume credits.
claims.quote: Experiences such as creating an automated solution with natural language, previewing and testing an agent, and generating and creating agent evaluations all consume credits.

claims.claim: Microsoft has not identified which harness the new comparison uses.
claims.quote: Searched: "multi-grader comparison" admin enable default permissions licensing credits harness; site:learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-copilot-studio "multi-grader comparison". Read the roadmap, evaluation results/API, preview introduction and billing overview; no harness assignment found.

claims.where: Cost and licensing; Governance controls; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Feature-specific extra charges or metering for multi-grader comparison are not published; the low cost assessment is limited to known preparation and review effort.
claims.quote: Searched: "multi-grader comparison" license pricing Copilot Credits. Opened agents-experience/billing-credit-overview and agents-experience/analytics-agent-evaluation-intro; they describe evaluation credit use but do not establish this comparison's harness, additional charge or rate.

claims.claim: Existing runs are compared in Copilot Studio at agent > Evaluation > Recent test results > test run > Compare with > comparison run.
claims.quote:
In your agent's Evaluation page, under Recent test results, open the test run you want to use as the base for the comparison.
Select the Compare with dropdown, and then select the time and date of the test run you want to compare with the currently open test results.

claims.claim: The printed Power Platform API POST operation runs an evaluation for the specified test set.
claims.quote: POST https://api.powerplatform.com/copilotstudio/environments/{EnvironmentId}/bots/{BotId}/api/makerevaluation/testsets/{TestSetId}/run?api-version=2024-10-01

claims.claim: GET of the evaluation testruns/{TestRunId} resource returns run details and results.
claims.quote:
GET https://api.powerplatform.com/copilotstudio/environments/{EnvironmentId}/bots/{BotId}/api/makerevaluation/testruns/{TestRunId}?api-version=2024-10-01
Purpose: Retrieve the details of an evaluation by using the runId for your target evaluation run.

claims.claim: Existing evaluations are maker-facing and can be started by selecting Evaluate at the end of creating or editing a test set.
claims.quote: At the end of creating or editing a test set, select Evaluate.

claims.claim: Blocking the Microsoft Copilot Studio connector through a data policy prevents existing evaluations using user authentication.
claims.quote: To prevent agent makers from adding event triggers to their agents or running automated evaluations by using an authenticated account, configure a data policy that blocks the Microsoft Copilot Studio connector.

claims.claim: Data policies are reached in Power Platform admin center through Security > Data and privacy > Data policy.
claims.quote:
On the sidebar, select Security, and then select Data and privacy. The Data protection and privacy page opens.
Select Data policy. The Data policies list appears.

claims.claim: Existing evaluation access can be granted through agent sharing and the agent viewer sharing role.
claims.quote: If you're the agent owner and want to grant access only to the Evaluation page of your agent, share the agent and enable the agent viewer sharing role.

claims.claim: Existing evaluations run with the currently signed-in user profile.
claims.quote: Evaluations and connections used by tools run with the currently signed-in user profile.
claims.fix: Replace the sentence with 'In the preview new agent experience, evaluations and connections used by tools run with the currently signed-in user profile.' The separately cited standard-harness API article says that without mcsConnectionId the evaluation runs without authentication.

claims.claim: The linked evaluation-methods page lists available methods for existing evaluations.
claims.quote: When you create test sets, choose from different test methods to evaluate your agent's responses. Each test method has its own strengths and suits different types of evaluations.
